She remained silent for a moment after he finished speaking.
"So, your choice?" Rex asked with his hand raised.
Linda clenched her fists while taking a deep breath.
"I knew it... my cheetah instinct never betrays me at all...
Bryan is indeed a piece of shit."
"I want to say I’m sorry to her," she said.
"His wife."
Rex said, "I thought you might."
"She didn’t do anything wrong," Linda said, "and she’s been living with something I had some part in, even if I didn’t know I did."
Rex said, "That’s a fair way to look at it."
She stared at the river.
Her stomach growled again, this time quieter, like a body politely asking for sustenance and beginning to lose its patience.
Growwlllll...
Linda felt embarrassed when she couldn’t control her stomach, and he chose to stay silent about it, hoping that Rex didn’t hear it.
"Poor you," Rex said sarcastically.
"Maybe I have some spare change on me to help ease that hungry stomach."
Rex looked at the coins in his pocket.
They were the ones he had gotten from people who had seen him in the northern district during the evacuation and had pressed them into his hand.
They were the ones he had gotten from walking through the residential neighborhoods that morning.
He put them on the wall of the embankment that was between them.
Linda saw them.
Then she turned to face him.
"There’s a food stall two streets to the east." Rex said, "They’re open all morning and make good flatbread."
She looked at the coins, then at him with the look that someone gets when they get something that isn’t charitable in its manner but is generous in its effect.
It was the kind of giving that didn’t require the receiver to show gratitude in a certain way.
"Why?" she asked, which was the honest answer.
"I didn’t deserve free money like this..."
"But..." Then she looked suspicious of him.
"Don’t tell me you’re no different than Bryan by giving me money just to do something lewd."
"Don’t be so fucking stupid... it’s all because you didn’t eat," Rex said, "and...
I have more than I need this morning, and it seems like the right thing to do."
"O-Ohh..." Linda then realized that Rex might be different and intriguing.
"You’re rather weird, but I respect it.
She picked up the coins with the careful speed of someone who had learned how to get help without making things hard.
"Thank you," she said.
"I’ll pay you back someday, when I get a job."
Rex said, "You don’t have to."
"I will anyway," she said, and the ears moved to the front, which meant that something had been decided.
Rex stared at the river.
"The Silver Rest Inn," he said.
"On the main street, two blocks from the eastern gate..."
"They’re looking for additional staff, and the owner is the woman whose husband you were just handling, and she knows about the situation and holds you blameless for it."
For a moment, Linda was very still.
Rex said, "That’s not a joke."
"I know," she said.
"I can tell when people are joking."
She held the coins tightly in her hand and gazed at the embankment stone.
Her thoughts raced in a manner akin to someone analyzing every possible angle, arriving at the same conclusion from each perspective.
"I want to apologize to her first," she said.
"Before anything else."
Rex said, "That’s the right order."
[LINDA LYSANDRA — DESIRE LEVEL: 0 → 69/100]
"W-what...?
A huge raise just like that...?" Rex thought.
"Is it because of the money I gave her?"
[TARGET WAS EASY TO PLEASE]
’Ahh... got it...’
I also want to thank you for what you did to Aethelgard." Linda said this with her tail starting to wave around.
"You honestly saved my life back then, and to be honest...
I already know who you really are."
She then laughed.
"Hehehe~!
I can’t believe I could meet a real hero like you who dares to sacrifice himself for everyone here!"
"Receiving this money from you confirms that you truly are a good and reliable human," she continued, her eyes sparkling with admiration.
"Your kindness is something I’ll never forget.
Rex listened with the enthusiasm of someone whose theory had once again proven correct through its application.
He hadn’t done anything significant.
’What a great fucking coincidence...
I didn’t realize how many people I saved back then, but of course, if she’s one of them...’
’I can tell that she’s definitely an obvious target.’
He had given correct information, useful help, and the kind of attention that made someone feel like they were being considered a person instead of a group of people.

The number on the screen indicated that she had apparently seen him in the northern district during the evacuation and recognized him as the person who had moved toward the blast instead of away from it.
Rex remarked that reaching sixty-nine desire from a complete stop in under twenty minutes was quite an impressive accomplishment for the morning.
He pushed himself away from the wall.
"First, eat something," he said.
"Then come to the Silver Rest.
I’ll be there."
Linda stared at him.
"Thank you," she said, and it was the short version that meant what it said.
"You say ’thank you’ a lot, you know," Rex sighed.
"I’m tired hearing it."
"Well, you deserve it, anyway."
Rex nodded once and walked back to the inn in the nice morning light, thinking about what he would do the rest of the day.
When Rex came back in to the inn, Marceline was at the bar in the position she used when she was managing a lot of things at once and had set herself up to do it well.
She looked at Rex when he walked in, and the look on her face answered the question she was about to ask.
"She’s on her way," Rex said.
"You’re really bringing her here?"
"Yeah, she wanted to apologize."
"Apologize...?
She doesn’t need to..." Marceline put down the glass she had been cleaning.
" When?"
"About an hour," Rex said.
"She wanted to eat first."
Marceline nodded, and for a moment she looked like someone who was getting ready for a conversation that wasn’t going to be fun but was going to be necessary and therefore going to be done well.
Marceline asked, "How is she?"
Rex thought about the embankment wall and the coins and the way the ears had gone to the forward position when she decided she would pay him back.
"She’s someone who’s been in a difficult situation she didn’t cause," Rex said, "and she’s been handling it with more class than the person who put her there."
For a moment, Marceline looked at the top of the bar.
"I knew it... demi-humans are having a hard time finding a job here, and now I feel like she doesn’t need to apologize at all."
"Yes."
"I’m going to tell her she doesn’t have to."
"She’s going to do it anyway," Rex said.
"She decided."
The corner of Marceline’s mouth moved in the specific way it moved when she encountered something that produced an unexpected version of warmth.
"Alright," she said.
"Then I’ll let her."
She picked up the glass again and resumed polishing it.
Rex made his way to his usual table and ordered the late breakfast that Mara had kept warm for him.
The morning continued to unfold at the Silver Rest.

chapters.title: Chapter 241. Linda is Going to Work With The Inn with One Condition? (Bryan is Cooked!)
paragraphs: It took Linda Lysandra just under an hour to get there.

She entered with the confidence of someone who had made a decision and was committed to following through rather than second-guessing herself. The fact that she had eaten was evident in her posture, and her ears were pointed forward.
She looked at Marceline across the common room.
Marceline looked at her.

The apology that followed was brief and direct, carrying the essence of something carefully crafted during the hour between the embankment and the inn’s front door. Linda recounted her actions, expressed her uncertainties, and shared what she would have done differently had she known everything.
She presented her thoughts without soliciting a specific response.
"I’m sorry... I didn’t mean to be his affair because I just thought that he was single and wanted to pay me as his maid."
"But it turns out that every payment he gave me just led to me doing some strange things for him, and I learned from one of his other affairs that he was already married."
Marceline listened attentively to everything Linda shared. Once Linda finished speaking, Marceline set aside what she was holding and walked around the bar.
In a surprising gesture, she hugged Linda briefly, offering the warmth that Marceline reserved for moments when she felt she had made a positive decision about someone.
"Poor girl... that bastard almost stole your innocence." Marceline patted her head as one would do to a child.
Rex started at them with a blank expression. ’Yeah... innocence... with a massive badonkers like that.’
"You didn’t do anything that needs my forgiveness," Marceline said. "But I’ll give it anyway if it helps."
"He didn’t take..." Marceline whispered close. "...your virginity, right?"
"No! Of course not!" Linda shook her head. "But he once showed me his thing, and it was so disgustingly small!"
"And what I mean is, I don’t want to be with someone like him!"
"My body is not something he could buy!"

They both stepped back and looked at each other with the interest of two people who had been brought together by a situation and were now deciding whether there was something worth building on from that connection.

Marceline held her own cheek. "Good to hear it then... many women are stupid enough to grab that money just so that they can satisfy his desire, knowing that he doesn’t have anything that’s worth worshipping."
"H-Huh...?" Linda looked confused.
"Anyway, she needs a job so that her stomach can’t make a loud noise," Rex said from his table, where he had been eating breakfast and not paying attention to them.
"R-Rex...!" Linda shouted at him.
Marceline stared at him.
"The inn needs staff," Rex said, still occupied with his breakfast. "You said so yourself."
"I did say that," Marceline said. "With Mara’s situation, I will be running the evening service alone."
She stared at Linda.
"Do you have household experience?" Marceline asked.
"Three years in the eastern provinces," Linda said. "Kitchen and general service.
Marceline nodded, as if she were finishing an evaluation that had come to the right conclusion.
"The room rate is covered by the position," Marceline said. "The pay is weekly."
"The hours are variable during reconstruction, but they’ll settle when the city does."
Linda looked at her, and the look she gave Marceline was like something that had been tightly wound for three months and was just now allowed to loosen a little.
"Yes..." Linda said. "Thank you so much, ma’am."
"Just call me Marceline."
Marceline looked like she was doing a practical task, which was how she dealt with things she felt strongly about but chose to do so through efficiency rather than expression.
"However, I still believe you need to earn this job by doing me a favor."
"Sure. I will do anything to pay for all my guilt."
After that, she leaned slightly toward Linda and whispered something that wasn’t meant for the common room.
Rex noticed Linda’s reaction from the corner of his eye. She froze immediately, her ears twitching to gauge the situation before slowly turning to face him.

"I want you to help me teach my husband a lesson..." Marceline whispered to Linda, her gaze fixed on Rex. "I can’t forgive him for his actions... especially since he’s gone so far as to spend all of our savings."

"I want to divorce him tonight, but I want it to be the most excruciating divorce he has ever experienced... and that charming guy right there is going to help me." Marceline turned back to Linda, sensing her intimidation. "You’re in on this too, right...?"
"Y-y-y-y-yes...!" Linda nodded as fast as she could, where the fur from her ears and tail started to get tensed up.
Rex looked her in the eye and smiled a little, as if to say that he had been in on the plan from the start and wasn’t going to act like he hadn’t.
"Oh yeah... she’s fucking dangerous alright, and it’s because I train her enough."
Linda glanced at him, then at Marceline, and finally at the common room as a whole, as if to confirm the details of the place she had just agreed to live in.
Her ears went back to the front.
She nodded very slowly and very clearly until Marceline backed off so she wouldn’t get scared.
Rex went back to eating breakfast with a satisfied smile. ’Just you fucking wait, Bryan...’
’You’re fucked for sure.’
Then Marceline said to Linda with a motherly smile, "Welcome to the Silver Rest, Linda."
"We’re going to spend a lot of fun times together~!"

The night proceeded as usual at the Silver Rest: it was warm, well-organized, and exuded the competence that Marceline and Mara had instilled through their relentless hard work, which had become almost invisible once firmly established.

Linda navigated the service rotation swiftly and efficiently, like someone who had extensive experience in this line of work. She didn’t need to learn anything new; the familiar environment made it all second nature to her.

Her ears followed the sounds in the common room like cat types do when they’re learning about a space. By the second hour, she had the layout memorized in the way she moved—direct paths instead of learning paths.

Garrett was in great shape, in the state of mind of someone who had just heard great news and was three hours into not being able to stop thinking about it. This made him both easier and harder to deal with as a kitchen staff member.

Mara took care of him with the patient warmth she brought to everything she did. Mara’s movements throughout the evening had a distinct quality, different from her usual manner, reflecting the way she carried information in her body that altered the meaning of her actions.

Bryan Bancey spent most of the night in the private dining room, working on what he said were supply chain accounts. Rex’s Foresight confirmed that he was writing letters, putting them aside, and then writing them again.
Rex took note of this and went on with his night.
Around the ninth hour, he went upstairs, washed, and changed. He had been lying down for approximately twelve minutes when he heard footsteps in the hallway.
Three sets of footsteps were moving in a coordinated manner, indicating that they had discussed their approach beforehand.
The first set was the heavier one, Bryan’s, moving from the private dining room toward the couple’s quarters, which was the room at the end of the corridor.
The second set was much lighter and faster. It came in behind Bryan’s with the precision of someone who had been waiting for this exact moment.
The sound that followed was brief and distinct: a muffled noise that occurred when someone exceptionally quick placed a bag over another person’s head before they could comprehend the situation.
Bryan stopped walking.

There was a brief moment of surprise and struggle, followed by the sound of someone being firmly pushed in a direction they didn’t want to go, like a cheetah-like demi-human who was faster than a normal human and had made a choice about this.
Rex heard it from his room.

A little while later, a door closed with a distinct sound from inside the private dining room. Following that, a silence settled over the room, as everyone inside focused intently and refrained from making any noise.
Rex stood up, fixed his clothes, and walked to the private dining room.
He unlocked the door.

Bryan Bancey sat in the chair at the head of the table, a position he might have preferred under different circumstances. Linda had procured a chain from a source Rex chose not to question, using it to secure his wrists to the chair’s armrests.
A cloth arrangement covered his mouth so that he couldn’t talk loudly enough to be heard through the inn’s walls.
His eyes were moving around the room in a way that showed he was trying to figure out the whole situation before he said anything.

Marceline stood before him, clad in a third robe—neither the working robe nor the comfortable one. Her hair cascaded down, and her arms were crossed, presenting an air of someone who had meticulously arranged everything to convey exactly what she intended, allowing the moment to speak for itself.
Linda stood to the right of Bryan’s chair with her arms at her sides and her tail moving slowly and purposefully, as it did when she had finished something and was ready for the next thing.
When Rex walked in, both of them looked at him.
Rex looked at Bryan.
Bryan looked at Rex with the eyes of a man who had been having a terrible day that was showing no signs of improvement.
Marceline looked at Rex with the look she had been building up to since the morning. It was the look that had been prepared specifically for this exact situation.
Rex smiled.
"Hello, Bryan," he said pleasantly.
"I believe we haven’t been properly introduced."

paragraphs: Rex walked into the room with a confident, almost threatening step. He looked around for a second before seeing Bryan, who was tied to the chair and looked shocked and scared.
Linda stood still to the side, her tail slowly moving back and forth. And there was Marceline, looking beautiful in a robe that sparkled in the candlelight.
She had her arms crossed and a fierce look of determination on her face. "I forgot to introduce someone who’s going to live in this inn for his entire life."

"And... he’s also my affair if you want to call it that." Marceline chuckled. "His name is Rex Rexilion... and he’s super hot, charming, and reliable... unlike someone who goes out with our saving money to pay women!"
"Well, well, well," Rex said, his voice dripping with fake sympathy. "Bryan, is it...?"
"I’ve heard a lot about you, and... I have to say, you don’t look as impressive as I thought you would." Rex laughed. "But... I guess that’s to be expected, given the situation."
"You’re buying those women probably because you’re such a pathetic piece of shit who’s insecure about himself."
He walked around the chair slowly, like a wolf stalking its prey. Bryan’s eyes followed him as his body fought against the chains that held him.
Rex could see the anger brewing behind those eyes and the need to lash out and get back some sense of power. But for now, they had him at their mercy.
Marceline stepped forward, and her heels made a loud noise as they hit the wooden floor. She moved in close to her husband, so close that their faces were only a few inches apart.
Her eyes were full of rage that seemed to burn hotter than any fire. "You see, my stupid husband..."

"...Bryan, I’ve been waiting a long time for this moment," she said in a low, dangerous voice. "It’s taken me a long time to make you understand how angry I am, how furious I have been since the day I found out about your affair."

"It all makes me think that we’re married just to waste all of our money and time..." Marceline slapped his face hard. "You thought you could use me and control me like a pawn in your sick fucking games!?"
Bryan couldn’t respond because his mouth was still covered with a cloth.

She stood up straight, her hands making fists at her sides. "But now, now you will pay for every cruel word, every callous act, every single moment of pain and humiliation you have inflicted upon me!"
"I have promised myself that this day... THIS DAY... will be a day you will never forget!"
"A day that will be seared into your memory for the rest of your miserable life."
Marceline turned to Rex with a fierce smile on her face. "I know that I can count on you with this one, my dear Rex..."
"I want you to make him scream in pain, Rex," she said, her voice full of hate. "Make him beg for mercy and ask for death to come quickly because he has to see everything!"
Bryan starts resisting, but then Rex snaps his fingers, and his face gets hit with a telekinetic force that surprises him. "Be a good boy, and watch the whole thing without resisting.
"But... if you keep resting with more force, then I might as well see your pain through it," Rex smirked.
"Yeah, that’s it! I want to watch and enjoy every second of his pain," Marceline said, her eyes wide with a crazed intensity. "Make it hurt, Rex...!"
"Make it fucking hurt so bad that he forgets his own name and everything else except the horrible pain of being at the mercy of a man like you!"
"Alright, I get it... and don’t worry." Rex cracked his fists. "This is my kind of shit right here."
Rex turned to Linda and grinned wickedly. "Linda, move this little asshole who’s sitting helplessly in his guest’s chair to Marceline’s room."
"Don’t you dare ask any question about this situation," he said, his voice dripping with false politeness. "He deserved all of this, right...?"

Linda nodded, her eyes shining with excitement as she held on to the back of the chair. Together, they lifted it, with Bryan still tied up and helpless, and carried him out of the private dining room.
Bryan’s heart raced as he walked down the hall, realizing how bad things were. When they got to Marceline’s room, he already saw his wife standing at the foot of her grand four-poster bed.
The room was dark, and the air was thick with a sense of doom.
Marceline’s eyes were full of lust as she looked at Rex. "Hope you’re enjoying the show we’re going to put on for you, bastard."
"Focus your eyes on a real man’s body," she said, her voice ringing out like a gunshot. "And see how I want to worship every inch of the man who will make my husband pay for his sins."
Rex didn’t think twice. He slowly began to unbutton his shirt, revealing inch by inch the muscular expanse of his chest.
He never took his eyes off Marceline, observing the emotions that flickered across her face: anger, anticipation, and a deep, abiding desire.

"Would you look at him, Rex?" Marceline said as she walked around the chair and ran her fingers along Bryan’s shoulders, chest, and bound arms. "Look at the pathetic creature who thought he could control me and break the sacred vows we made to each other."
Bryan squirmed in his chains, his face red with anger and shame. Rex could see how his chest heaved with each ragged breath and how hard his muscles were working against the chains.
He could hear Bryan’s muffled cries for help, which were drowned out by the thick fabric of the gag. "Hahahahaha! I can see it clear..."
"Shhh, don’t struggle so much." Rex said in a dark, honeyed voice, "You wouldn’t want to get tired before the real fun starts, would you?"
Marceline stopped and looked Rex right in the eye. "Would you help me punish my husband, Rex...?"
"Fuck yeah! Count me in, baby."
